clue.text: Oscars distribution is over

indicators.note: a distribution spreads things around, so the letters are dealt out in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A report that the handing out of film awards has finished for the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Across and over are synonyms as prepositions of crossing, as in walking across or over a bridge.

clue.text: Alias I had to drop, unfortunately

indicators.note: something that has to drop falls out, so one letter is removed from the word

parts.note: taken as written
the letter itself, the one that goes

explanation.surface: Someone regretfully having to abandon a false name they had been using.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the I out of ALIAS to leave ALAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection of regret, used where unfortunately would be in a sentence.

clue.text: Artist gives thanks once again to model for knocking

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
ta is informal British for thanks
the thanks repeated
the Model T Ford

explanation.surface: A painter repeatedly thanking a sitter, as if at a studio session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once again' doubles the thanks. The Model T was Ford's famous early car, so model = T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat-a-tat is the sound of repeated knocking at a door, an imitative word for the noise.

clue.text: Son to drag off fare dodger?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
to tow is to drag along
off, as in gone off, means away

explanation.surface: A parent hauling a child off after catching them riding without a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition as an example: a stowaway hides aboard to travel without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: A stowaway hides on a ship or plane to travel free, so is one kind of person dodging payment for passage.

clue.text: Queen, in fact, beside river for a break

indicators.note: in places the first item inside the following word

parts.note: taken as written
R for Regina, Latin for queen
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A statement that a queen, sitting by a river, is in fact taking a holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside FACT to make FRACT, and the Ure, a crossword favourite among rivers, follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A fracture is a crack or break, especially in a bone, so the noun matches a break.

clue.text: These American political adherents are undemocratic!

definitions.text: These American political adherents are undemocratic!

parts.words: These American political adherents are undemocratic!
parts.note: surface reading: an accusation that some US partisans oppose democracy
setter's reading: they are literally not Democrats, being members of the other main US party

explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark signals the pun: undemocratic means not belonging to the Democratic Party, rather than hostile to democracy.
explanation.definitionFit: In US politics the two main parties are Democrats and their rivals, so supporters of the rival party are by definition non-Democrats.

clue.text: Vessel, unknown, is tricky

parts.note: a craft is a boat or ship
y is a mathematical unknown

explanation.surface: A mystery ship that is proving difficult to deal with.
explanation.definitionFit: Crafty and tricky are synonyms, both meaning cunning or sly in getting one's way.

clue.text: Disclose United Nations' position over dry land

parts.note: the standard abbreviation
earth is the ground, the land as opposed to sea

explanation.surface: A demand that the UN reveal its stance over some disputed territory.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, one piece positioned over another simply comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth is to dig up and bring to light, so figuratively to reveal or disclose.

clue.text: Tip: this is the limit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the end point or furthest part of something
second meaning: the utmost degree or extreme

explanation.surface: Someone offering advice and then declaring that things have gone too far.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the far end of a limb or object and the most extreme point or degree.

clue.text: Writer absorbed in taut horror movie

indicators.note: absorbed in says the word sits soaked up inside the following text

parts.note: letters run across the two words
surface padding completing the picture of a film

explanation.surface: A novelist engrossed in a tense scary film.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is one who writes books, so author and writer are synonyms.

clue.text: Father's back with relative, it's obvious

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
a parent is a close relative

explanation.surface: Dad has returned with a family member, and the situation is plain to see.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparent means plainly seen or evident, a direct synonym for obvious.

clue.text: A curious fact: there's a mysterious seat on French street

parts.note: a synonym
the butt, or bottom, is what one sits on
rue is French for street

explanation.surface: A puzzling report of an odd bench found on a road in France.
explanation.walkthrough: Seat is used in its sense of the backside, not a chair.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase introduces a surprising fact that is nonetheless real, so it names a curious fact.

clue.text: Young redhead produces a mild spice

parts.note: green means young and inexperienced
ginger is a nickname for a red-haired person

explanation.surface: A young red-haired person turning out a gently flavoured seasoning.
explanation.walkthrough: Ginger is everyday British slang for someone with red hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Green ginger is fresh, undried ginger root, milder than the dried spice.

clue.text: Homely dish cooked: gotta piece?

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A hungry diner asking if they can have some of the simple supper just made.
explanation.walkthrough: Cottage pie is a British dish of minced beef topped with mashed potato.
explanation.definitionFit: Cottage pie is plain home cooking, a comforting family meal, so homely dish describes it.

clue.text: Fish and French carrier in a holdall

parts.note: a carp is a freshwater fish
et is French for and
a bag carries things

explanation.surface: A fish and a French shopping bag stuffed into a larger travelling bag.
explanation.walkthrough: 'French' tells you to translate 'and' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpetbag is a travelling bag originally made of carpet fabric, a type of holdall.

clue.text: That interminable one from the Far East?

indicators.note: interminable means without an end, so the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A weary complaint about some endless person who comes from distant Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: THAT loses its last letter, then I follows. The question mark admits Thailand is in South-East Asia, loosely the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai describes things belonging to Thailand, a country often loosely grouped within the Far East.

clue.text: Love Hero's young man had for this flowering shrub

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
in Greek legend Leander swam the Hellespont nightly to his lover Hero

explanation.surface: A romantic tale in which a woman's beau declares his love for a plant.
explanation.walkthrough: Hero is not a brave man here but the priestess of Greek legend whose lover was Leander.
explanation.definitionFit: The oleander is an evergreen Mediterranean shrub with showy pink or white flowers.

clue.text: Wild display of red, indigo or turquoise, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

parts.note: first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A description of an exuberant splash of bright colours.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase 'a riot of colour' makes the definition apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A riot is an unrestrained, lavish profusion, as in a riot of colour, so a wild display.

clue.text: Newly divorced, about to leave but went too far

indicators.note: newly suggests something made afresh, so the letters are put in a new order
something told to leave goes away, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
c for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A recently divorced person on the point of departing yet overstepping the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove C from DIVORCED, then rearrange the remaining seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To overdo something is to take it to excess, so overdid is the past tense meaning went too far.

clue.text: Certainly acts as though incapable of error

definitions.meaning: first meaning: without any doubt, unfailingly

definitions.text: acts as though incapable of error
definitions.note: describes the manner of acting; the answer is the adverb
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the way one behaves who can never be wrong

explanation.surface: Someone who behaves with total confidence, as if they could never make a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads as how such a person acts: they act infallibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Infallible means unable to be wrong, so the adverb means both unfailingly, hence certainly, and in an error-proof way.

clue.text: Direct route taken by a flier?

definitions.text: Direct route taken by a flier?

parts.words: Direct route taken by a flier?
parts.note: surface reading: an aircraft or pilot's straight flight path
setter's reading: the flier is an insect, said to fly straight back to its hive

explanation.walkthrough: Flier suggests a pilot or plane, but the insect that makes honey is meant; its supposed straight homeward flight gives the idiom.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the most direct route anywhere, from the belief that the insects fly straight home.

clue.text: Make new ascent to the viewpoint

indicators.note: making something new means rebuilding it, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Climbers urged to try a fresh climb up to a lookout spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Viewpoint suggests a scenic lookout, but here it means an opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: A stance is a position or attitude on an issue, so a point of view.

clue.text: A different Chevalier crest for powered tool

indicators.note: a different version of the words means their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A knight adopting a new coat-of-arms emblem as a symbol of his powerful weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: A chevalier is a knight; his crest is a heraldic emblem. Only the fodder's fourteen letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: An electric shaver is a mains- or battery-driven device for shaving, so a powered tool.

clue.text: In the works Marlowe revised, we are diminished

indicators.note: something in the works is inside the machinery, so the word lies within the following text

parts.note: letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: An editor complaining that revising a playwright's texts has made them smaller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diminished' describes the contraction: the two words shortened to one with an apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: A contraction is a shortened form, so the contracted version of the two-word phrase is literally reduced.

clue.text: Repartee degenerates as one gets older

parts.note: to go bad is to degenerate
growing older is going on in age

explanation.surface: A grumble that witty banter declines as people age.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the wordplay as 'goes bad in age'.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is light, playful banter, a near synonym for witty repartee.

clue.text: Publicity may lead to anger, then respect

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement, a piece of publicity

indicators.note: the lead of a word is its front, so only the opening letter is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
a synonym

explanation.surface: Fame can stir resentment at first and esteem later on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a verb meaning cause, but it picks the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to hold them in high regard, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Good tragedy, perhaps, is one of many useful devices

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the word is only a possible form, so its letters may be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone musing that a fine drama might count as one of a range of handy tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Gadgetry is a collective noun for gadgets, small handy contraptions, so it covers many devices.

clue.text: Border, reportedly, has very cold weather

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so a word with the same sound is wanted

parts.note: a frieze is a decorative band or border along a wall

explanation.surface: A frontier region suffering a bitterly cold spell.
explanation.walkthrough: A frieze is a decorative strip along the top of a wall or room.
explanation.definitionFit: A freeze is a period of frost and sub-zero temperatures, so a spell of very cold weather.
